project_name: The Material Form of the Heart Sutra
english_name: Material Form of the Heart Sutra
core_concept: Count the times Tang Sanzang chants the “Heart Sutra” throughout Journey to the West, along with their scenes and the emotional fluctuations of the surrounding plot, then present them in wave form on an exhibition wall using an extremely fine gold thread
design_principle: The crests represent the calm after chanting; the troughs represent the extreme fear encountered around the chanting; the gold thread ultimately winds into a giant “heart”-shaped void projection
deeper_meaning: This is a physical model of “how faith resists external shocks”

sutra_chanting_records.context: The Crow's Nest Chan Master transmits the “Heart Sutra” to Tang Sanzang · first contact
sutra_chanting_records.key_phrase: Form is not other than emptiness; emptiness is not other than form

sutra_chanting_records.context: Meets the Yellow Wind Monster · Wukong's eyes are injured · Tang Sanzang chants and prays
sutra_chanting_records.key_phrase: Mind free of hindrances; because of no hindrances

sutra_chanting_records.context: Thrice defeats the White Bone Demon · Wukong is banished · Tang Sanzang chants alone
sutra_chanting_records.key_phrase: Without terror; far from inverted delusions

sutra_chanting_records.context: Rescues the Black Rooster king · stays the night at Baolin Monastery · Tang Sanzang chants to soothe
Blocked at the Heaven-Reaching River · stays the night at Chen Village · Tang Sanzang chants to seek passage
Sweeps the pagoda in Jisai Kingdom · chants at midnight · meets the Nine-Headed Insect
sutra_chanting_records.key_phrase: All Buddhas of the three times, by relying on Prajñāpāramitā

sutra_chanting_records.context: Saves the children's hearts and livers · Tang Sanzang chants in anger
sutra_chanting_records.key_phrase: No suffering, origin, cessation, or path; no wisdom and no attainment

sutra_chanting_records.context: The Dharma-Destroying Kingdom kills monks · Tang Sanzang disguises himself · chants the Heart Sutra at night
sutra_chanting_records.key_phrase: Mind free of hindrances; because of no hindrances

sutra_chanting_records.context: Near Spirit Mountain · the Indian princess seeks a husband · Tang Sanzang chants to steady his mind
Arrives at Spirit Mountain · sheds his mortal body at the Lingyun Crossing · Tang Sanzang chants for the last time

wave_statistics.deepest_valley: Bhiksu Kingdom · saving the children's hearts and livers
wave_statistics.highest_peak: Spirit Mountain · Buddhahood, return to zero
wave_statistics.trend: The wave gradually flattens, finally returning to zero, reflecting the maturation of the mind

sculpture_design.wave_length: Each segment about 1.2m · corresponding to one chanting
sculpture_design.lighting: Top light + side light · giving the gold thread a faint shadow
sculpture_design.projection: The gold thread ultimately winds into a “heart”-shaped void · projected onto the floor
sculpture_design.interaction: As viewers approach, the heart-shaped void flickers like breathing

artistic_statement: Faith is not unchanging calm, but a repeated tug-of-war between fear and stability; the gold thread's wave is the materialization of that tug-of-war
